target_customer: Gen Z and young millennial savers in India, many first time investors
problem: Young Indians do not save or invest because it feels boring. Fello gave users one game token per rupee saved, to play daily and weekly games with a chance to win cash prizes, while the money went into digital gold and other assets.
business_model: Consumer savings and investing app; revenue from partner products and spread, not stated in sources
product_category: Game based savings and investing app

founders.name: Manish Maryada
prior_employers: Traditional finance firms and early stage fintech startups (unnamed)
education: Texas A&M University Mays Business School, Master's in Finance

founders.name: Shourya Lala
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. A 2021 MicroSave article calls him a computer engineer with fintech software experience.

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app combining UPI payments, mutual fund and digital gold integrations and a games layer, with partners ICICI Prudential and Augmont per MicroSave. Standard fintech engineering with regulatory partners.

defensibility.rationale: Gamified savings is easy to copy and relied on referral incentives. Partner products such as digital gold are commodity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied Fello in the sources. By 2024 and 2026 the product shifted toward gold, silver and fixed deposit investing, per Fello 2.0 coverage and the live site.

market_need_then: The YC description reports 250,000 users in 12 weeks with 92 percent referred and 88 percent first time investors. A 2022 interview and Inc42 report referral shares of 94 and 80 percent respectively, which indicates strong early pull.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful: save, play and win cash prizes weekly, with Tambola style games.

branding.brand_signature: Weekly game with a Rs 1 lakh prize pool tied to saving
branding.community_and_virality: Referral driven growth: the YC description says 92 percent of users were referred and Inc42 reported referral rewards up to 500 rupees per referral. Press includes Inc42, YourStory, VCCircle and CNBC TV18 per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: A playful invented name and a distinctive game mechanic drove referral heavy growth to 800,000 users per a cxotoday headline, but no logo or community evidence was found.

pivots.to: Investment app centered on digital gold, silver and fixed deposits
pivots.why: Not stated. A 2024 IBSi report on Fello 2.0 and the live site show the product moved toward investing; gamification is less prominent.

outcome_analysis: Fello grew fast on referrals, raising a 1 million dollar seed in November 2021 and 4 million dollars in January 2023 led by Courtside Ventures. YC lists it as Inactive, but the website is live with gold, silver and fixed deposit products and blog posts dated April 2026, so the company appears to operate. Its focus shifted from games to investing.
notes: YC status Inactive conflicts with a live site; exit type is none. Founding year not found (a MicroSave article dated August 2021 already describes the app), so founded_year is null. The January 2023 round is labelled other because Inc42 calls it a fresh round without a stage; one aggregator calls both rounds seed. Total raised is not stated by Inc42; aggregators list 5 to 5.6 million dollars. YourStory pages returned 403 and were not used. A secondary source in search results says the name stands for Hello to Finance but the page was not opened, so name_origin is null. Competitors Jar, YottaSavings and Prizepool are named in the January 2023 Inc42 article, which is about 11 months after the batch, so they are not listed as of founding. The Fello 2.0 pivot date is the year of the IBSi report.
